A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VILA-M3 study, with readable text, tables and figures that can be matched reliably. v2 includes Supplementary Material, Sections 6–9, which is referenced but not included in the supplied v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original medical VQA, classification and report-generation experiments, general-purpose benchmark evaluations, and expert-feedback and dataset-balancing ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds statistical comparisons, expanded training analyses and disease-specific report-generation results in its supplement.

M1.justification: The four-stage training framework, expert-triggering procedure, segmentation/classification feedback and model architectures remain unchanged. The supplement explains previously described data preparation and expert integration without establishing a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: The medical and general-purpose task coverage remains the same. Table 8 identifies MSD and TotalSegmentatorV2 as sources for the already described CT expert-training stream; this documents existing coverage rather than establishing an expansion. Additional evaluations reuse the existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1 and 3–6 remain unchanged, including Med-Gemini, VILA-1.5, TorchXRayVision, GPT-4o and the report-generation baselines. The new statistical tables analyze the existing GPT-4o comparisons.

E3.justification: The supplement extends the balanced/unbalanced comparison to 8B and 13B models trained for two epochs and introduces disease-stratified evaluation of the best-performing 40B report-generation model. Main-text splits, metrics and training settings remain unchanged; newly supplied preprocessing and GPT-4o retry details are disclosures rather than demonstrated protocol revisions.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the reported analyses: balancing comparisons beyond 3B, full training curves including 40B, epoch-wise results across all model sizes, and disease-specific effects of expert feedback (Figures 8–11 and Table 13). These extend the narrower balancing, convergence and expert-feedback analyses in v1.

E5.justification: Section 8.4 introduces McNemar chi-square tests and class-specific p-values comparing all four VILA-M3 variants with GPT-4o on both classification datasets (Tables 11–12), using a 0.05 threshold. v1 provides no corresponding inferential statistics. This does not establish additional training runs or seed-based uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results, but v2 adds substantial supplementary outcomes, including significance tests, expanded balancing/epoch results and disease-specific report scores. For example, new Table 13 reports expert versus non-expert GREEN scores of 36.56 versus 35.93 for atelectasis, but 34.97 versus 37.23 for consolidation. These are newly reported comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version develops new formal theory or proofs. Table 10 supplies fitted parameters for the empirical scaling law already discussed in v1; it adds numerical documentation rather than a new mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about expert-guided medical VLMs, combined task capabilities, hybrid 2D/3D integration and open-source support. The headline approximately 9% and 6% improvements are unchanged.

C2.justification: The supplement adds explanations of model-size and convergence behavior, GPT-4o refusals, exceptions to overfitting for report generation, and condition-dependent benefits of expert feedback. Some interpretations overreach: Section 8.5 generalizes third-epoch deterioration across model variants, although Figure 11 shows several improving 3B results.

D1.justification: v2 supplies sampling frequencies and counts, expert-training dataset sources, Llama-3.1 report-curation prompts and examples, GPT-4o prompting/retry details, and inference memory, throughput and context limits. It also adds explicit code, model and demo links. Much of this information was only referred to as supplementary material in v1.

R1.justification: The same 60 cited works remain after reference renumbering, and the related-work discussion preserves the same positioning relative to medical VLMs, expert models and agentic systems.

P1.justification: The main narrative and Sections 1–5 remain largely verbatim. Changes include shortening redundant abstract wording, revising author and contribution labels, updating cross-references and organizing the added supplement into Sections 6–9; there is no extensive rewrite of the existing argument.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different title, abstract, typography, header and caption template, relocates existing figures and tables, and adds Tables 7–13 and Figures 7–11. The expanded plots and supplementary displays materially change presentation beyond pagination alone.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency and evidential support by supplying previously unavailable preparation details, statistical tests and diagnostic analyses. However, errors limit the gains: Table 7 totals disagree with its listed rows, the Section 6.2.3 cleaning example reverses an effusion finding, and the expanded overfitting interpretation exceeds Figure 11's evidence. The paper becomes easier to scrutinize, but the new material does not provide an unqualified substantial improvement in reliability.
